definitions.explanation: A frog — a small jumping amphibian that lives in or near water. Usually written in katakana as カエル, though the kanji {蛙|かえる} also exists.

examples.english: There is a frog in the pond.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るとカエルが{鳴|な}く。
{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}、よく{田|た}んぼでカエルを{捕|つか}まえた。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often caught frogs in the rice paddies.

notes:
Frogs are a familiar part of the rural Japanese landscape, especially in and around rice paddies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カエルが{鳴|な}く: frogs croak
- {雨蛙|あまがえる}: tree frog (lit. rain frog)
- カエルを{捕|つか}まえる: to catch a frog

RELATED WORDS:
- {井|い}の{中|なか}の{蛙|かわず}: a frog in a well — someone with a narrow view of the world (uses the older reading かわず)
